newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Universal sees good 97 prospects.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Universal sees good 97 prospects.

text.p: Cyprus's Universal Life on Wednesday forecast an increase in profits in 1997 after "excellent" 1996 results.
The insurance company reported a 33.7 percent increase in 1996 pre-tax profits for the year ended 31 December 1996, up to 2.01 million pounds ($3.9 million) from 1.5 million the previous year.

"Last year was a difficult year for us, as it was for the entire insurance market," Executive Director Andreas Georgiou told a news conference. "Issues relating to the economy and competition were some of the factors. I believe 1997 will be a better year."
The company will propose a 20 percent, or 10 cents per share, dividend to shareholders at the annual general meeting scheduled for June 18.
Last year the dividend was 40 percent, but it was calculated on a smaller issued capital base and in reality the 1996 dividend is higher, he said.

Georgiou said the company fared well from the increased competition from banking organisations which branched out into the insurance sector. During during the same year the company took a 50.2 stake in the Yialousa Savings Bank, subsequently named Universal Savings Bank.

"The penetration of banks into the insurance sector and the need to offer all types of banking and insurance business to clients made us speed up our own involvement in the banking sector," said Georgiou.
He said Universal Savings was now working on expanding its network of branches to all towns of the island.

In 1996 the Greek branch of Universal, Universal Life (Hellas) bought issued share capital in CIGNA Insurance Company Hellas SA and renamed the company Universal Life (International) AAEZ. It has offices in Athens, Salonika, Patras and Crete.
"This purchase has boosted the portfolio of the company and the prospects of expansion into Greece," Georgiou said. ($=0.51 pounds)
